notes: A running account of where things stand by these headlines, revised after each edition rather than added to. Every version is kept.
Written by the model from the narratives, not from the headlines. It is a reading, not a record.
standing: With the US midterms due on 3 November, Axios reports Benjamin Netanyahu pressing for a broad attack on Iran once the vote is over, while Donald Trump says talks with Iran are going well and Iran's foreign minister sets conditions for resuming them. Brent crude fell 2% to $111, and Yemeni government forces reported 1,272 strikes on the Houthis in a day. Israel's Likud says a black cloud hangs over the Knesset result as the elections chief opens an inquiry into irregularities, and Reuters reports Trump aides planning to govern without Congress if Democrats win. Bulgaria's Gyurov conceded the presidential runoff, and India's opposition called 50,000 people to demand the election commission chair resign. Italy's budget guarantees pensions up to 25,000 euros, Britain's John Healey promises a smaller benefits bill and Spanish economists put a sick self-employed worker at 180 euros for the month, while India's no-cost EMI loans and the largest crypto theft, blamed on North Korea, were joined as hidden costs of paying; there was no narrative today on the AI share falls, France's protests, Poland's tribunal or Russia.
moved: The Iran thread turned away from fuel taxes. On 2 November Brent fell to $111, Trump said talks were going well, and Netanyahu was reported wanting a strike after the US vote, so the thread now turns on whether strike or talks follow 3 November.

The contested-count thread returned after two editions without a narrative, placed there by the Chronicle's judgment: the doubt now comes from governing sides, Likud in Israel and Trump's aides in the United States, while Bulgaria's challenger conceded.
Two threads began: the cost of new ways of paying reaching the payer as interest, data or theft, and budgets that protect pensions and salaried staff while the self-employed and claimants get less.
No expectation set by any narrative was kept or failed since the previous Chronicle, so no thread's direction has yet been tested against a later headline.
silent: Drones in war, last carried on 30 October, has now gone three editions without a narrative and is silent. Ukrainian combat robots appeared inside the AI thread on 1 November, so the subject may be running under other joins rather than ending.
Former leaders between courts and amnesty has had no narrative since 29 October; nothing on Yoon Suk Yeol or Jair Bolsonaro appeared on 2 November, which may be the collection's sample on a weekend.
Brazil's election and the United States has had no narrative since 27 October and no Brazilian headline in the last three editions.
Public schemes falling short, begun on 27 October, was not revived by the new budgets thread, though the two touch the same ground of households left with less by public provision.

threads.label: Iran war, oil prices, taxes and the US vote
threads.text: On 26 October the join was the Gulf running talks and strike preparations side by side; on 27 October it was the Hormuz shock at the pump, then jet fuel, asphalt and subsidies. On 29 October it reached mortgages; on 30 October reports ran towards easing; on 31 October Brent rose to $117.64 and the rise reached Italian inflation and pay rounds; on 1 November Turkey raised its fuel tax and talks were reported stalled. On 2 November the fuel-tax argument was absent: Brent fell 2% to $111, Trump said talks were going well, Iran's foreign minister set conditions, Axios reported Netanyahu pressing for a broad strike once the midterms end, and Yemeni forces reported 1,272 strikes on the Houthis in a day. The edition's case against says only Netanyahu's request ties the war to the vote.
threads.direction: Having spread from the pump to borrowing, wages and taxes, on 2 November it returned to its first question, strike or talks, now reported as timed to the US vote on 3 November.

threads.label: Brazil's election and the United States
threads.text: On 26 October Brazil's vote was read as a script in Buenos Aires, Madrid and Nairobi. On the morning of 27 October Trump called the election rigged; by that evening, after Lula's run-off win, the United States was the common party in Flávio Bolsonaro's exit, Lula's warning of persecution, about 300 US soldiers in Colombia and Machado's return to Venezuela. Its events then ran under wider joins: Flávio Bolsonaro's arrival in the United States and an amnesty plan for Jair Bolsonaro on 29 October, and Flávio's letter declaring himself president on 30 October. Nothing from Brazil appeared on 31 October, 1 November or 2 November.
threads.direction: It moved from how Brazil's vote is read abroad to Washington's part in what follows, then was taken up under wider joins and fell silent.

threads.label: AI companies' listing, land and lawsuits
threads.text: On 26 October the join was an AI company listing the end of the world as a risk factor in its prospectus and the market buying the shares. Early on 27 October an edition followed data centres to county level, where land, grid and water requests were refused, and that morning Anthropic filed for a record US share listing as Elvis Presley's rights holders sued it over 200 songs. Data centres split into their own thread on 29 October. No narrative on listings or lawsuits has followed in six editions; the falls of Alphabet and Intel from 30 October to 1 November were carried in the AI spending thread.
threads.direction: It went from the prospectus to the ground and the courts, then fell silent as its market side was carried under the AI spending thread.

threads.label: Young people's protests and their policing
threads.text: On 26 October the join was young people in public squares; on 27 October students struck or occupied buildings in France, Mexico, India and Italy. After three silent editions the Chronicle revived it on 31 October, when protests called for the same weekend met a ban in La Rochelle, perimeters in Rochefort and Saintes and negotiation in Lisbon. On 1 November the edition carried the link forward: France deployed 70,000 security personnel for a third weekend, Toulouse diverted metro and buses, German coverage asked whether France's violence would reach its Gen Z protest, and protesters were detained in Poland. No headline reported a negotiation or a demand. No narrative carried it on 2 November; whether France deploys 50,000 or more for a fourth weekend stays open until 9 November.
threads.direction: It has moved from youth as a political image to student strikes and then to policing reported as officers counted and routes diverted, with the protesters' demands unreported.

threads.label: State housing drives and housing protests
threads.text: On the morning of 27 October one narrative joined Egypt, Indonesia and Tamil Nadu expanding housing through states and employers with Portugal investigating police conduct at housing protests, and the part property funds play. No narrative has followed it in five editions. Mortgage rates appeared in the oil thread on 29 and 30 October, and on 31 October Lisbon's housing camps and the Rossio demonstration appeared in the protest thread.

threads.label: Public schemes passing costs to households
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. In six countries a public scheme meant to cover a cost was reported as falling short: Canadians paying for private surgery from savings and GoFundMe, German adult children billed for parents' care, Lucknow's subsidised generic pharmacies short of medicines, a Bangladeshi antivenom programme lacking funds, compensation claims from 50,000 Australians over unlawful Centrelink suspensions, and doubt over a Mexican voluntary pension scheme. The case against noted that several of these stories have run for years. No narrative has carried it since; the budgets thread begun on 2 November touches nearby ground but did not cite it.

threads.label: AI-made faces and files in checks
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. Nigeria's electoral commission is investigating suspected AI-generated photos in the voters' register, New Zealand job seekers report being ignored as AI-written applications flood employers, an Australian court passed the first sentence under deepfake laws without jail, and fashion models face AI copies of their image. The join is that a plausible picture or document now costs little to make while checking it still takes a person's time. No narrative has carried it in the editions since.

threads.label: Broadcasts and films removed over offence
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. A Chinese platform dropped Racing-Real Madrid and La Liga broadcasts were suspended after a remark by Mbappé, an Indian court ordered a documentary on Adani and Modi taken down, a Korean drama faced calls to halt over a Gwangju episode, and Neil Young sued to stop Trump rallies using his songs. Three of the headlines were the same Mbappé story. No narrative has carried it in the editions since.

threads.label: AI spending: profit, sell-off and who gains
threads.text: Begun on 29 October with Samsung and CHPT profits on data centre demand beside Norwegian, Finnish and Russian disputes. On 30 October it reached US growth of 3.4% credited to AI investment and the results of Amazon and Alphabet. On 31 October Alphabet had its biggest fall on record, Intel lost 29% and Taiwan's state funds and central bank bought against record foreign selling. On 1 November no state buying was reported; the edition read the same falls as AI money landing narrowly, with 700 Micron staff in Taiwan paid five years' salary and Chinese results led by AI computing. No narrative carried it on 2 November, and its expectations on further Taiwanese buying, Korean support and a 3% index fall remain open.
threads.direction: It has moved from profit and local objection to national growth and a share sell-off, and on 1 November to how few firms the spending reaches.

threads.label: Former leaders between courts and amnesty
threads.text: Begun on 29 October. South Korea's special counsel again sought, and by one report won, a death sentence for former president Yoon Suk Yeol over his martial law declaration, while in Brazil Alcolumbre planned an amnesty for Jair Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro reached the United States with Trump's consent. Spain's Zapatero, India's Azam Khan and Indonesia's anti-corruption law also appeared. No narrative has carried the court cases since; Azam Khan's release reappeared on 1 November in the constitutions and courts thread.

threads.label: Failed safety systems and operator blame
threads.text: Begun on 29 October and marked tentative by its own edition. A high-speed collision near Urda in Spain, which other headlines say killed 68 people, followed at least 15 warnings about faulty signalling; a JR train in Japan overran a station when its driver was drowsy and its automatic braking did not act; Bangladesh, Manila's airport and Mexico's networks had failures of grids, servers, cameras and internet. Only the Spanish and Japanese cases had a stated cause. No narrative has carried it since.

threads.label: Vote counts and rolls as contested ground
threads.text: Begun on 30 October with Flávio Bolsonaro declaring himself Brazil's president, Gadi Eisenkot accusing Netanyahu of delegitimising Israel's result, a widening federal inquiry into the Alaska vote, deletion forms against Muslim voters in Delhi and a disputed governorship in Imo, Nigeria. After two editions without it, a narrative the edition did not link returned on 2 November and the Chronicle placed it here: Likud says a black cloud hangs over the Knesset result as Israel's elections chief opens an inquiry, Reuters reports Trump aides planning to govern without Congress if Democrats win, India's opposition calls 50,000 people against the election commission's chair, Bulgaria's Gyurov concedes the runoff, and the Alaska dispute is reported ended. Its case against says the US report concerns divided government, not refusing a count, and that a collection two days before a US vote overweights such disputes.
threads.direction: It has narrowed from anyone contesting a count to doubt raised by governing sides in Israel and the United States, on the eve of the US vote.

threads.label: Drones in war, numbers and arms production
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined drones cutting power, guarding a lake, carrying the wounded and being sold. After three silent editions drones returned on 30 October, by the Chronicle's judgment, as a matter of numbers: a shortage of Ukrainian interceptors, a record raid shutting Moscow and St Petersburg airports, Finnish anti-drone training, Ukrainian loans to arms makers and Lithuanian conscription from 2032. No narrative carried drones on 31 October, 1 November or 2 November, and it is now silent; Ukrainian combat robots appeared in the AI thread on 1 November.
threads.direction: It moved from the drone's many uses to the number of drones and the factories and conscripts states are raising to match them, then fell silent.

threads.label: Russia shunned by Europe, courted elsewhere
threads.text: Begun on 31 October. European ministers refused to stand beside Sergei Lavrov for the G20 photograph and Poland's foreign minister told him 'enough', while US and Russian foreign ministers discussed coordination at APEC, Washington weighed lifting sanctions on a Putin associate, Russia signed 53 documents at its Africa summit and Nigeria moved to replace a 1967 air agreement with Moscow. Washington also approved 500 Patriot missiles for Ukraine. The case against says the Europeans still attended and the African deals renew old ties. No narrative carried it on 1 or 2 November; its expectations, a US easing of sanctions and a European objection to one, are still open. One more edition without it turns it silent.

threads.label: Constitutions and courts as political battleground
threads.text: Begun on 1 November and marked tentative by its own edition. In Poland the president and Donald Tusk's government fight over control of the Constitutional Tribunal, with tensions outside the building and protesters detained; Egypt's Masrawy asks whether the constitution should be amended; a Portuguese column says Madeira should not wait for the national revision; and in India a case is filed against Mallikarjun Kharge while the Enforcement Directorate waits for Azam Khan's release. Its case against says only Poland's is a crisis. No narrative carried it on 2 November; India's protest against the election commission and Israel's inquiry went to the contested-count thread, which sits close to this one.

threads.label: Money leaving and states offering discounts
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined savings and fortunes moving into dollars, gold and trusts with states answering by amnesties and discounts meant to bring the money back into view. No narrative in the editions since has followed it, so it stands as a single observation. The amnesty bills of 29 October concerned convictions, not tax or hidden money.

threads.label: AI buyouts and dangerous manual work
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative set office workers being paid to leave as AI takes their tasks against labourers still dying in ditches, fields and collapsed buildings. No later narrative has carried it. On 1 November the AI thread touched nearby ground, with Micron staff payouts in Taiwan and robot guards in Jiangsu said to replace five people, but no narrative revived this join.

threads.label: Rites counted before the days of the dead
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined reports that measured the rites of late October and early November before they happen: numbers of hosts, incense sticks, costumes and the strain on worshippers' knees. No narrative has carried it since. On 31 October the only trace of Halloween was the cost of sweets inside the wage narrative, and on 1 and 2 November, All Saints' and All Souls' Days, no narrative returned to it.

threads.label: European household readiness and borrowed deterrence
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined European advice that households should be able to last 72 hours on their own with European states seeking cover from nuclear warheads they do not own. No narrative in the editions since has returned to it. Finnish anti-drone training and Lithuanian conscription on 30 October went to the drones thread, and Europe's stance towards Russia on 31 October to its own thread.

threads.label: One football night watched worldwide
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined coverage of a single football night that drew attention across many countries at once. It was tied to one event and no narrative has carried it since. Football returned on 27 October only as a broadcasting dispute in the removal-over-offence thread.

threads.label: Courts re-sentencing past events
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined courts re-sentencing events of 1979 and 1996 with a library removing material from 2026, treating them as revisions of the record. No narrative has carried it since. The former-leaders, contested-count and constitutions threads touch nearby ground, but none re-sentences an old event.

threads.label: New ways of paying and their hidden costs
threads.text: Begun on 2 November and marked tentative by its own edition. The Hindu explains that India's no-cost EMI is a loan presented as free; Yle reports Finnish shoppers annoyed by data collection but keeping their loyalty cards; Bangladesh launches a QR code for person-to-person payments while Jawa Pos defends Indonesians who still pay cash; the FBI, reported by DW, blames North Korea for the largest cryptocurrency theft in history, which Yle says hit Binance; and impostors defraud older people. The join is that the visible fee has gone and the cost sits in a loan, a purchase record or an account the payer does not control. Its case against says these have different causes and that India's central bank has warned about such instalments since at least 2013.

threads.label: Budgets protecting pensions over working-age incomes
threads.text: Begun on 2 November. Italy's budget promises no pension cuts up to 25,000 euros and faster severance for civil servants, with 17 million euros for floods in three regions and 2 million more a year for a 'freedom income' for women. Britain's John Healey promises the benefits bill will come down, Spanish economists say a self-employed worker on sick leave can have 180 euros for the month, and Russia reminds savers how to draw pension savings. The join is that income tied to age or a salaried contract is protected while income outside it is trimmed. Its case against says Italy's is the only budget and Healey is the defence secretary. It sits near the silent public-schemes thread of 27 October, which the narrative did not cite.

withdrawn.held: AI companies' share listings, the copyright suit against Anthropic and county refusals of data centre land, grid and water formed one thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 29 October data centres returned on their own, as profit for Samsung and CHPT and as planning and security disputes in Norway, Finland and Russia, with no listing or lawsuit in view. The land and power question is running apart from the companies' finance and courts, so the merge no longer holds.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war's price rise was moving outward from the pump to central bank rates and loan contracts, with the war named less often at each step.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the reports ran the other way: Washington pressing Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries and sending Tehran a peace proposal, Israel's pump price set to fall, Russia budgeting on $50 oil and US mortgage rates down for two weeks. The war was named directly again, and the costs were reported as easing more than spreading.

withdrawn.held: The data centre question was running apart from the AI companies' finance, as a matter of land, power and security.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the data centre thread itself turned to finance: US growth credited to AI investment, Amazon's spending and Alphabet's fall in market value, with no planning or security dispute in that edition. The split of threads stands, but the separation of data centres from company finance does not.

withdrawn.held: On 30 October the Iran war's costs had turned towards easing, with Washington pressing for a lower oil price before the midterms.
withdrawn.undone: On 31 October Brent rose 2.4% to $117.64, Italy's inflation reached 5.4% and the price rise was argued over in pay rounds and tax relief in several countries. The easing reading did not last a day, and the earlier withdrawal of the outward-spread reading now looks premature.

withdrawn.held: The AI share sell-off was moving towards losses partly taken on by Taiwanese public money, through its state funds and central bank.
withdrawn.undone: On 1 November no state buying was reported, and the same thread was read as AI money landing on a few chip and computing makers, with Micron staff payouts and Chinese results led by AI computing. The public-money reading rested on one edition and is not carried as the thread's direction.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war thread had turned to which governments carry the fuel price and which take more of it as revenue, with US-Iran talks stuck.
withdrawn.undone: On 2 November no fuel-tax argument appeared, Brent fell 2% to $111, Trump said talks were going well and the thread was about whether a strike or talks follow the US vote. The who-pays reading rested on Turkey's single tax rise and is not carried as the direction; its expectation of a second government raising a fuel tax is still open.

caseAgainst: This Chronicle rests on nine editions over about 146 hours, still with none stamped 28 October, and no expectation set by any narrative has yet been kept or failed, so every direction here is a reading of headlines, not a test of one. Only one of today's four narratives carries a continuation link; I placed the election narrative in the contested-count thread myself, and the brief that asks for continuity may produce such joins as much as the world does. Today's collection was gathered two days before the US midterms and soon after Israel's election, so it will overweight election disputes and anything that can be tied to the vote; the Iran narrative's own case against says only Netanyahu's reported request ties the war to the vote, and a 2% move in oil is not an election effect. The oil thread has now been read as spreading, easing, spreading, who pays and strike-or-talks in five versions, which may reflect which headlines each collection caught more than any change in the war or the market. Both new threads lean on weekend explainers, one Italian budget and a defence secretary's promise. The AI, protest, constitutions and Russia threads had nothing today, which on a Sunday may be the sample. My earlier versions led with the war, and I have led with it again.
line: On 2 November 2026, the eve of the US midterms, Brent falls to $111 as Netanyahu is reported pressing for an Iran strike after the vote and Trump says talks go well.
revision: The Iran thread's direction turned from fuel taxes to strike or talks after the US vote, and its previous who-pays reading is withdrawn. The contested-count thread was continued by the Chronicle's judgment, two threads began on hidden payment costs and on budgets protecting pensions, and the drones thread fell silent, leaving eight live; the standing was rewritten around the eve of the midterms.
